diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer appears hung or silently stalled. Its container is running and healthy, but it has emitted no consumer-event metrics and no logs in at least 30 minutes, so it is not committing offsets on provider-events and its lag has passed 100. Possible mechanisms: a blocked poll or handler, a lost partition assignment, or a stuck DB or Kafka connection that the health check does not detect. A deploy or crash is unlikely: nothing changed or restarted in about 13 hours. This is open: payment-confirmer also shows no consumer-event series in c2, so the cause could be broader, such as broken telemetry export to otel-lgtm or a wrong metric name in my query. I could not check per-group lag, payment-confirmer logs or traces.

evidence.shows: No deploys or setting changes for about 784 minutes. ledger-consumer runs LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, the normal settings, so a config change is not the cause.
rate(klaxon_consumer_events_total) returned no series over the last 30 minutes for any consumer or outcome: no events processed, or none reported.
All containers, ledger-consumer included, are running and healthy with 0 restarts since 2026-10-17T22:25, so there is no crash loop. The health check passes while nothing is processed.
ledger-consumer wrote no log lines in the last 30 minutes, not even errors or retries. This fits a hung process or broken telemetry export, not a consumer failing loudly on a bad message.

proposed_fix.summary: First confirm: query klaxon_kafka_consumer_lag by consumer group to see if only the ledger group lags; check whether payment-confirmer and webhook-receiver are logging, to rule out a broken telemetry pipeline; take a stack dump of ledger-consumer if possible; check Postgres for locks. If only ledger-consumer is stalled, restart it so it rejoins its group and resumes from its last committed offset. Watch lag fall and the event rate return, then run money_check(wait=true) to confirm each event is posted exactly once and the ledger balances. Follow-up: make the health check verify poll and commit progress, not just liveness.

diagnosis.blast_radius: A restart briefly pauses ledger posting and triggers a consumer-group rebalance. Messages after the last committed offset are redelivered; the idempotent handler should prevent double-posting, and money_check should verify it. payment-confirmer, webhook-receiver and payments-api are separate and unaffected. If the real cause is telemetry or the DB, the restart will not clear the lag.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: A restart changes no code or config, so there is nothing to revert. If ledger-consumer does not recover or lag keeps growing, stop it, leave its committed offsets as they are, and escalate. Then investigate Kafka group state, Postgres locks and connections, and the otel-lgtm export path.
